title: Sumo Wrestling with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D sumo wrestling game using Three.js with particle effects. Generate a single HTML file with all code inline.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 8, 12) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.0.
- Create a circular ring (dohyo) as a cylinder (radius 5, height 0.3) with a sandy/tan color (#D2B48C) centered at origin. Add a white border ring on top (torus, radius 4.8).
- The background should be a dark gradient or solid color (#1a1a2e).

## Wrestlers
- **Player wrestler (left):** Load the 'DamagedHelmet.glb' model using THREE.GLTFLoader from CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). Scale it to (0.8, 0.8, 0.8) and place at (-2, 1, 0). This represents the player's sumo wrestler head/body.
- **Opponent wrestler (right):** Create a sphere (radius 0.7) with a red metallic material at (2, 1, 0). Give it simple AI movement.
- Both wrestlers should have a visible "mass" represented by a larger semi-transparent sphere around them (radius 1.2).

## Physics & Movement
- Player moves with WASD keys. W=forward(+z toward opponent), S=back, A=left, D=right. Movement speed: 0.08 per frame.
- Both wrestlers have position clamped within a radius of 6 from center (slightly beyond ring edge).
- Implement collision detection between wrestlers (distance < 2.0). On collision, apply a push force: the wrestler with more momentum pushes the other back.
- A wrestler is "pushed out" when their distance from center exceeds 4.8 (ring edge).
- The opponent AI should slowly move toward the player, with speed 0.03 per frame, and occasionally charge (speed 0.1) every 3 seconds.

## Particle Effects
- When wrestlers collide, spawn 20-30 particles at the collision point. Particles should be small spheres or points with yellow/orange colors that fly outward and fade over 1 second.
- When a wrestler is pushed out of the ring, spawn 50 large red particles in an explosion effect.
- Dust particles should continuously emit from wrestlers' feet (bottom) when they move - small brown particles drifting upward.

## Game State & Rounds
- The game has rounds. Each round ends when one wrestler is pushed outside the ring (distance > 4.8 from center).
- Track scores: playerScore and opponentScore. First to 3 wins.
- After a round ends, wait 2 seconds then reset positions to starting spots.
- Display a "ROUND START" text for 1.5 seconds at the beginning of each round.

## HUD/UI
- Display player score (left) and opponent score (right) at the top of the screen using HTML overlay divs.
- Show a "FIGHT!" button (id='startBtn') that begins the match. Before clicking, wrestlers don't move.
- Show round number in the center top (id='roundDisplay').
- Show game status text (id='statusText') for messages like 'Round Start!', 'Player Wins Round!', 'Game Over!'.
- Add a "Reset Game" button (id='resetBtn') that appears when the game is over.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- gameStarted: boolean (true after clicking FIGHT)
- roundActive: boolean (true during active gameplay in a round)
- currentRound: number (starts at 1)
- playerScore: number
- opponentScore: number
- playerPosition: {x, y, z} - current player position
- opponentPosition: {x, y, z} - current opponent position
- playerInRing: boolean (distance from center <= 4.8)
- opponentInRing: boolean
- collisionCount: number (total collisions this game)
- activeParticleCount: number (currently visible particles)
- gameOver: boolean
- winner: string ('none', 'player', 'opponent')
- lastCollisionTime: number (timestamp of last collision)
- playerDistanceFromCenter: number
- opponentDistanceFromCenter: number

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Wrestlers move on a flat plane (y=1). Collision pushback is proportional to relative velocity. Ring boundary is radius 4.8 from center. Movement speeds: player 0.08, opponent 0.03 (normal) / 0.1 (charge). Particles obey gravity (y acceleration -9.8) and fade over time.
